images.title: Four layers of 16 make 64
images.purpose: Shows a cube of edge 4 split into 4 layers of 16 unit cubes, so it holds 4 cubed, which is 64, unit cubes.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. Four flat layers of unit cubes stacked with small gaps, in the centre, with three short labels.
images.exact_structure: Exactly 4 identical square slabs, each a 4 by 4 layer of exactly 16 unit cubes in flat oblique view, stacked one above another with a small gap between slabs. Slabs alternate teal (#0072B2) and amber (#E69F00) from the bottom, starting with teal. 64 unit cubes in all. Beside the top slab: 16 cubes. A brace along the right of the stack: 4 layers. Below the stack, centred: 4³ = 64. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: A cube of edge n is n layers of n × n unit cubes, so it holds n³ of them.
images.description: Shows a cube of edge 4 split into 4 layers of 16 unit cubes, so it holds 4 cubed, which is 64, unit cubes.

image_decisions.why: Separating the layers lets students count 4 × 16 and see why cubing is not tripling.
